Consider three writers: (a) a writer that appends a random UUID each time\u2014neither idempotent nor safe under retry; (b) a writer that appends a deterministic content hash each time\u2014safe (duplicates are detectable and removable) but still not idempotent (append of the same hash twice still yields two log entries before dedup); (c) a writer that checks the log for an existing entry with the same key before appending\u2014this makes the compound check-then-append operation idempotent in effect, but it requires a read-before-write that breaks the append-only model's single-direction discipline. The append-only log requires property (b): safety through deterministic identity, not the idempotency of (c), because (c) introduces a read path that contradicts the append-only discipline.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log supports atomic compare-and-append (conditional append only if key absent), then writer (c) becomes feasible without a separate read path, and the distinction collapses","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the deduplication pass during replay is itself non-deterministic (e.g., depends on arrival order rather than key ordering), then writer (b) is not actually safe","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Writer (a) fails because duplicates are indistinguishable from new events. Writer (c) achieves idempotency by reading the log before appending, but this introduces a read-before-write coupling that violates the append-only principle and creates a race condition under concurrent writers. Writer (b) is safe because every retry carries a deterministic key; the log accepts all appends (preserving append-only discipline) and a separate deduplication pass during replay filters duplicates. The key insight is that safety is achievable within the append-only model, while true operation-level idempotency requires a read path that breaks it.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
